flowRoot.flowPara: Running a standard experiment:
1) Execute the desktop link: "Link Experiment" (sh: otree_link_experiment)
This script links your otree project folder to the hidden $HOME/.oTree location that is used by the nginx webserver as project root.
It copies the folder Templates/_rooms, containing this lab's econ101.txt to your project folder.
2) Execute the desktop link: "(Re)Start oTree" (sh: otree_restart)
The script asks
2.1) whether to run 'otree collectstatic'
2.2) whether to run 'otree resetdb'
and runs 'otree runprodserver'.

Note: If you run 'resetdb' the script creates a 7zipped backup of the current database in the folder DB_BackUps named "pg_TIMESTAMP.7z". It is highly recommended that you keep a copy of this database backup, too. If anything goes wrong you can still restore the database and data of the previous session from this file.
3) Open Chromium browser

By default Chromium launches on http://localhost:8000. For generation of external links that are NOT preconfigured in rooms, you need to connect via the external IP address. You can find the virtualmachine's external IP in the conky system monitor on the desktop.
4) Setup your "Rooms"
EconLab 101 is the preconfigured setting for this lab.
5) Now connect the clients
Run the script "Start_Chrome.bat" in the folder "Relaunch Chrome Clients" on the windows host machine's desktop.
Technical notes:
1) The system uses a load balancing Nginx webserver.

2) The Nginx webserver looks in $HOME/.oTree for the project root. 'Link Experiment' (sh: otree_link_experiment) creates a symlink from your project folder to this location providing Nginx with the necessary environment.

3) 'Postgres database server', 'production mode', 'authentication level' for otree are configured in $HOME/otree_environ_config and can easily be changed there. The user's .bashrc sources this script upon login or launching a terminal window. The desktop links separately each source this config file so that you can quickly switch between DEBUG and PRODUCTION mode.
4) The folder Templates/_rooms contains a preconfigured econ101.txt file that you might need to adapt to your lab's requirements. Otherwise your config might be overwritten upon launching otree.

5) HTTPS: If you require a secure web connection you need to create your own SSL-certificates via, e.g., letsencrypt or your host institution's IT department. The created certificates have to be configured in the appropriate nginx config file.
For this account it would be /etc/nginx/sites-available/default
6) Windows clients: Currently Windows based Chrome clients can only be launched remotely via 'psexec' from a Windows host machine. You can find a template set up in the folder
Templates/Relauch Chrome Clients.

7) Project Folders: ... need to contain a virtual environment folder called "venv". In case you copy a project to this image that does not contain a corresponding folder you can copy such a folder from a project created using 'Start New oTree Project' (sh: otree_startproject).
